stories.headline: Qualcomm signs first 5G cross-license with Huawei and buys some of its US AI and compute patents

key_facts.fact: On October 5, 2026, Huawei and Qualcomm announced a multi-year, broad patent license agreement with cross licenses covering 5G, compute, AI and networking.
key_facts.excerpt: [Shenzhen, China, October 5, 2026] Huawei and Qualcomm today announced a multi-year, broad patent license agreement that includes cross licenses to the companies' patent portfolios across a range of technology fields, including 5G, compute, AI, and networking

key_facts.fact: As part of the deal Qualcomm will buy certain Huawei US patents in compute, AI and networking; the transaction will close after regulatory approvals.
key_facts.excerpt: together with Qualcomm's purchase of certain Huawei U.S. patents in the areas of compute, AI, networking, and other technologies. This transaction will close following receipt of the necessary regulatory approvals.

key_facts.fact: Huawei says it is its first patent-licensing deal with Qualcomm covering 5G, and the first in which it licenses and assigns compute, AI and networking patents to the US chip designer.
key_facts.excerpt: The deal marks Huawei's first patent-licensing agreement with Qualcomm covering 5G technology, according to the Chinese company. It is also the first agreement under which Huawei licenses and assigns patents in compute, AI and networking technologies to the U.S. chip designer

key_facts.fact: SCMP says it is the first time Qualcomm has agreed to pay to license and acquire Huawei patents. The deal value was not disclosed. In 2020 Huawei paid Qualcomm $1.8 billion in back licensing fees to settle a dispute.
key_facts.excerpt: US chip giant Qualcomm has agreed to pay to licence and acquire patents from China's Huawei Technologies for the first time ... The value of the deal was not disclosed. The two tech powerhouses settled a dispute in 2020, with Huawei agreeing to pay Qualcomm US$1.8 billion in back licensing fees.

key_facts.fact: Huawei said the deal should lift the total value of its patent licensing agreements above $6.9 billion once completed. It follows a licensing deal with HP Inc announced in August.
key_facts.excerpt: Huawei said the deal is expected to push the total value of its patent licensing agreements to more than $6.9 billion once completed. ... The Qualcomm agreement follows a licensing deal with HP Inc announced by Huawei in August.

stories.headline: Musk confirms early talks with TSMC to build and run his Terafab chip plant in Texas

key_facts.fact: Late Friday, October 2, Culpium reported that TSMC was exploring ways to work with SpaceX's Terafab project. It called TSMC owning and operating the new factory the most likely scenario.
key_facts.excerpt: Late Friday I reported exclusively that TSMC was exploring ways to work with SpaceX's Terafab project. "The most likely scenario is for TSMC to try to own and operate the new factory," I wrote.

key_facts.fact: Musk confirmed the talks on X on Saturday, October 3: "Just discussions, but something may come of it." TSMC has not commented publicly.
key_facts.excerpt: Elon Musk confirmed the discussions early on Saturday, but did not elaborate. "Just discussions, but something may come of it," Musk wrote in an X post, while TSMC has so far remained tight-lipped.

key_facts.fact: Two structures have been described. In one, TSMC owns and operates the fab while SpaceX invests and/or commits to chip volumes. In the other, SpaceX holds a majority and TSMC supplies operations and process technology. The fab would serve only Tesla, SpaceX and xAI.
key_facts.excerpt: TSMC would own and operate the new semiconductor production facility, while SpaceX/Terafab could invest in the venture, commit to buying a guaranteed volume of chips, or combine both approaches. ... Another option would put SpaceX in control of the venture with the majority ownership

key_facts.fact: Intel is Terafab's only publicly named chipmaking partner, and Tesla has said it will use Intel's 14A process there. Intel shares fell about 4% premarket on Monday, October 5, to $114.43, while TSMC's US shares rose 1.8%.
key_facts.excerpt: Intel $114.43 premarket 7:21 a.m. ET, -$4.90 / -4.1% vs $119.33 Friday close. TSMC U.S. shares +1.8% to $481.23

key_facts.fact: Culpium reports that TSMC's rumored plans for a Texas fab complex are tied to its effort to support Terafab.
key_facts.excerpt: Culpium: Recent rumors of TSMC expanding into Texas are tied to efforts to support Terafab. Culpium: Collaboration with Intel on Terafab is not making progress.

key_facts.fact: On October 3, Musk also replied on X to a post calling TSMC's possible contribution to Terafab 'supplemental': 'A sufficiently large quantity is a quality all its own.'
key_facts.excerpt: A sufficiently large quantity is a quality all its own. ... QT @XFreeze: Anything TSMC contributes to Terafab would basically be supplemental

stories.headline: Schneider Electric agrees to buy PTC for $23.7B in cash, its largest acquisition

key_facts.fact: On October 5, 2026, Schneider Electric agreed to acquire PTC, a US maker of industrial design and engineering software, for $205 per share in cash. The deal values PTC's equity at about $22.6 billion and its enterprise value at $23.7 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: All-cash acquisition at $205 per share for 100% of the share capital of PTC, valuing PTC's equity at approximately $22.6 billion (€20.1 billion) - Implied Enterprise Value of $23.7 billion (€21.1 billion)

key_facts.fact: The price is a 42.3% premium to PTC's last close and a 46.1% premium to its 30-day volume-weighted average.
key_facts.excerpt: representing a 42.3% premium to PTC's last closing price and a 46.1% premium to the previous 30-trading days volume-weighted average share price prior to announcement

key_facts.fact: Schneider has a committed $25 billion bridge facility. It plans to fund the deal with about €5-6 billion of new equity and €16-17 billion of new debt. Closing is expected by Q3 2027, and PTC would owe a $700 million break fee in specified cases.
key_facts.excerpt: Closing is anticipated by Q3 2027 ... Schneider Electric has a committed $25 billion bridge facility and expects funding to combine an equity issuance of approximately €5 billion to €6 billion and new debt issuance of approximately €16 billion to €17 billion. PTC may owe Schneider Electric a $700 million termination fee

key_facts.fact: According to Bloomberg, it is Schneider's biggest acquisition to date and a push into the AI boom. The maker of electrical products adds engineering software for the automotive, aerospace and medtech industries.
key_facts.excerpt: Schneider Electric SE agreed to buy industrial software firm PTC Inc. for about $22.6 billion, stepping up its effort to tap into the artificial-intelligence boom with its biggest acquisition to date. The French conglomerate, which makes a suite of electrical products...

key_facts.fact: Closing requires approval from PTC shareholders and clearance under HSR antitrust rules and from CFIUS. The merger agreement was signed on October 4, 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: On October 4, 2026, PTC Inc. ... entered into an Agreement and Plan of Merger ... including expiration or early termination of the waiting period under the Hart-Scott-Rodino Antitrust Improvements Act of 1976, as amended, and approval by the Committee on Foreign Investment in the United States

stories.headline: Nvidia-backed Firmus to give half of up to $5.5B IPO to existing backers as demand exceeds offer

key_facts.fact: A book update sent on Monday, October 5, said Firmus Technologies plans to allocate about half of its US$5.5 billion (A$7.9 billion) IPO to a handful of existing backers. Indications of interest were 'well in excess' of the offer size.
key_facts.excerpt: Firmus Technologies plans to allocate about half of its $US5.5 billion ($7.9 billion) initial public offering to a handful of existing backers, according to a book update sent on Monday morning. Indications of interest ... were "well in excess" of the offer size

key_facts.fact: Shares are fixed at A$11, valuing Firmus at about $30.6 billion, nearly triple the ~$10.5 billion post-money valuation of its August round. Trading on the ASX is due to start October 23.
key_facts.excerpt: The company has fixed the share price at A$11 ($7.65), giving it a valuation of about $30.6 billion ... Firmus' valuation has nearly tripled since its August funding round, which valued the company at around $10.5 billion post-money.

key_facts.fact: It would be the second-largest Australian-listed IPO on record, behind Telstra's $10 billion sale in 1997. Banks now expect to close the institutional bookbuild on Thursday, a day early.
key_facts.excerpt: The planned share sale would be the second-largest Australian-listed IPO on record, behind only Telstra's $10 billion share sale in 1997. ... the banks now expect to close the institutional bookbuild on Thursday, a day earlier than the Friday close

key_facts.fact: Nvidia holds about 7.2% of Firmus, Coatue about 8.4% and Blackstone about 6.7%. Firmus is expected to carry about US$30 billion in debt, and some fund managers, including Blackwattle, said they will skip the offer.
key_facts.excerpt: Chipmaker Nvidia holds about 7.2% of the company, while technology investment group Coatue owns around 8.4% and Blackstone has a stake of approximately 6.7%. ... Firmus expected to carry about US$30 billion in debt ... Blackwattle Investment Partners said it did not intend to participate

key_facts.fact: Firmus designs and operates modular 'AI factories' using its own energy and cooling technology. It runs data centres in Melbourne and Singapore, and IPO proceeds are earmarked for GPUs for its Batam, Indonesia site.
key_facts.excerpt: Sydney-headquartered Firmus is an AI-infrastructure and cloud-services company that designs and operates modular AI factories using proprietary energy and cooling technology. It currently operates one data centre in Melbourne and one in Singapore.

stories.headline: Former Groq engineers sue its board, say Nvidia's $20B license deal shortchanged shareholders

key_facts.fact: Former Groq engineers and shareholders Benjamin Serebrin and Joshua Rubin sued in Delaware's Chancery Court on Friday, October 2, over Groq's 2025 deal with Nvidia. The complaint was unsealed on Monday, October 5.
key_facts.excerpt: Two former Groq shareholders are targeting the transaction in Delaware's Chancery Court, where their lawsuit against Groq's former board and CEO was unsealed Monday. ... The case is Serebrin v. Ross, Del. Ch., No. 2026-1291, complaint unsealed 10/5/26.

key_facts.fact: The suit alleges Groq's board transferred its core technology and top staff to Nvidia while leaving other shareholders with a diminished business, and that some investors could not vote on the deal.
key_facts.excerpt: Nvidia's $20bn licensing deal with Groq fleeced employees who were left out of the transaction, according to a lawsuit filed by two engineers who owned shares in the start-up. The legal complaint filed on Friday in a Delaware corporate law court...

key_facts.fact: The complaint describes a $17 billion license payment plus a separate ~$3 billion pool of Nvidia stock for selected engineers who joined Nvidia, up to about 200 people, including founder Jonathan Ross.
key_facts.excerpt: The transaction included a $17bn licensing payment plus a $3bn Nvidia stock bonus pool for key Groq engineers who joined Nvidia, affecting around 200 workers.

key_facts.fact: The suit alleges 'flagrant breaches of fiduciary duty' that 'cost Groq's stockholders billions of dollars.' Groq called the lawsuit meritless and said it will vigorously defend itself.
key_facts.excerpt: The Groq arrangement involved "flagrant breaches of fiduciary duty" that "cost Groq's stockholders billions of dollars," the suit says. ... "This lawsuit is meritless and we will vigorously defend ourselves against it," the spokesperson said.

key_facts.fact: The plaintiffs acknowledge that no Delaware precedent directly applies merger rules to a license-plus-acqui-hire deal. Separately, the Justice Department has reportedly been examining whether the deal was designed to avoid antitrust review.
key_facts.excerpt: The plaintiffs acknowledge there is no Delaware precedent directly applying merger rules to this kind of transaction. It also lands after the New York Times reported in September that the US Justice Department is examining whether the deal was designed to avoid antitrust review.

stories.headline: German robot-arm maker RobCo tops $1B valuation in $40M share sale, double January's mark

key_facts.fact: On October 5, Munich-based RobCo said it had passed a $1 billion valuation through a secondary share sale. Its CEO Roman Holzl has moved to the US to focus on the company's fastest-growing market.
key_facts.excerpt: German robotics maker RobCo on Monday said it had passed a $1 billion valuation and that its CEO Roman Holzl had relocated to the United States to focus on the company's fastest-growing market.

key_facts.fact: The Wall Street Journal reported that the transaction involved the sale of $40 million of shares.
key_facts.excerpt: The Wall Street Journal, which first reported Monday's transaction and valuation, said the transaction involved the sale of $40 million worth of shares.

key_facts.fact: Most of the stock was sold by employees rather than issued by the company. The valuation doubles the roughly $500 million set by RobCo's $100 million Series C in January, led by Lightspeed and Lingotto.
key_facts.excerpt: secondary share sale that raised $40 million, with most of the stock sold by employees rather than the company itself ... The transaction doubles the valuation RobCo reached in January, when it closed a $100 million fundraising round that put it at roughly $500 million

key_facts.fact: New investors Cherry Ventures and European Tech Collective, whose LPs include Wiz founders, bought in alongside existing backers Sequoia, Lightspeed and Lingotto.
key_facts.excerpt: Among the new investors are Cherry Ventures and European Tech Collective, a fund backed by limited partners that include founders of Wiz ... Existing investors Sequoia, Lightspeed, Lingotto and others also participated

key_facts.fact: RobCo is preparing a 2027 commercial launch of Alfie, its autonomous industrial robot, as it focuses on US manufacturing.
key_facts.excerpt: RobCo is preparing to launch Alfie, its autonomous industrial robot, commercially in 2027 as it doubles down on the US manufacturing market.

stories.headline: Oracle to take 10-20% of Wisconsin nuclear plant's output for OpenAI data center campus

key_facts.fact: On October 2, 2026, Oracle announced a commitment to subscribe to a portion of the Point Beach Nuclear Plant's output. It expects the move to save Wisconsin utility customers about $300 million in fuel costs.
key_facts.excerpt: AUSTIN, Texas, Oct. 2, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Oracle today announced a commitment to subscribe to a portion of the existing Point Beach Nuclear Plant's electricity generation, an action expected to save Wisconsin utility customers approximately $300 million in fuel costs.

key_facts.fact: Under the agreement with We Energies, Oracle can subscribe to 10-20% of the 1,200-MW plant's generation to power Project Lighthouse, the Port Washington data center campus it is co-developing with OpenAI.
key_facts.excerpt: an agreement that would allow Oracle to "subscribe" to between 10 percent and 20 percent of the Point Beach Nuclear Plant's electricity generation. Oracle will provide the carbon-free energy to Project Lighthouse, the data center campus in Port Washington that Oracle is co-developing with artificial intelligence firm OpenAI.

key_facts.fact: The subscription still needs approval from the Public Service Commission of Wisconsin.
key_facts.excerpt: Oracle's planned subscription to a portion of the Point Beach purchase power arrangement remains subject to approval by the Public Service Commission of Wisconsin.

key_facts.fact: OCI executive vice president Mahesh Thiagarajan said the commitment will benefit more than 1 million Wisconsin utility customers.
key_facts.excerpt: "Oracle is stepping up with a commitment that will directly benefit more than 1 million Wisconsin utility customers," said Mahesh Thiagarajan, executive vice president, Oracle Cloud Infrastructure.

key_facts.fact: Oracle also said it will fully fund Project Lighthouse's energy costs to protect ratepayers.
key_facts.excerpt: Oracle also said it will fully fund Project Lighthouse's energy costs "to protect ratepayers' electricity bills and support grid reliability."
